channel.title: IndieHOT — Indie Game Hot Topics
channel.description: IndieHOT collects indie game news from a set of public sources every day and scores it by rules: engines & tools, publishing & marketing, devlogs, industry & funding, events, reviews & postmortems. Only titles, one-line self-written summaries and outbound links are shown — no full text is republished.

item.title: Meta Quest Store Submission Guide for Developers
item.description: A practical guide for VR developers on getting through the Meta Horizon Store review, covering the performance, pause behaviour and data-declaration checks behind most rejections.

item.title: I built an unofficial Azur Promilia wiki with launch-day tools — here's the data model
item.description: A game launched worldwide today and its player-made wiki went live the same morning — here is how the site's launch-day tools and data model were built.

item.title: Game Audio Format & Magic-Byte Compatibility Matrix (2026): FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA & XWB
item.description: A 2026 reference table for identifying game audio containers from FMOD, Wwise, Nintendo and CRIWARE by their magic bytes, so you can pick the right decoder before trial and error.

item.title: Why our pool balls sped up mid-roll (and 3 other bugs from a browser pool game)
item.description: A postmortem of four unrelated bugs behind 'the physics feels wrong' in a hand-rolled three.js browser pool game: frame-rate-stepped physics, balls slipping through pocket mouths, AI freezing the game and shaders compiling mid-shot.

item.title: Game Audio Format & Magic-Byte Compatibility Matrix (2026): FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA & XWB
item.description: A 2026 compatibility matrix of game audio formats and their magic bytes — FSB5, WEM, BNK, BFSTM, HCA, XWB — with an open-source CLI that works fully offline.

item.title: Release candidate: Godot 4.8 RC 1
item.description: Godot 4.8 has entered the release candidate stage with all features locked in and known critical regressions fixed; the team invites production projects to try it after backing up, and asks the community to help test for any remaining major issues.

item.title: Grab the Best Black Friday Deals on 3D Tools, Assets & Courses
item.description: A roundup of Black Friday discounts on 3D tools, assets, and courses from Fab, the Unity Asset Store, Adobe, Reallusion, and more.

item.title: Curved ramps in a 2D physics engine, and the ball that looked like it was being hit 500 times a second
item.description: A devlog from the Rust physics engine Soliton on adding curved ramps properly — representing curves exactly so balls roll smoothly instead of bouncing hundreds of times a second.

item.title: I built a synthwave endless runner with Three.js
item.description: To learn 3D rendering, the author skipped the spinning-cube tutorial and built a neon-grid synthwave endless runner in the browser with Three.js — switch lanes, dodge obstacles, and it keeps speeding up.

item.title: A pre-export checklist for Blender textures (before Unity or Godot)
item.description: Missing textures in Unity or Godot are usually export mistakes, not engine bugs — this pre-export checklist catches them in Blender before they cost you a rework.

item.title: Data-Driven Units for a Turn-Based Strategy Game: A Schema Checklist Before Your Team Splits the Content Work
item.description: Turn-based strategy games multiply a few systems across dozens of units — this schema checklist helps teams lock down unit data before splitting the content work.

item.title: My AI game master lied about who was in the room. That bug became an agent-honesty checker.
item.description: An AI game master claimed a character standing next to the player wasn't there — and described a living companion as a corpse. That bug became an agent-honesty checker.

item.title: A pre-export checklist for Blender textures (before Unity or Godot)
item.description: Missing textures in Unity or Godot are usually export mistakes, not engine bugs — this pre-export checklist catches them in Blender before they cost you a rework.

item.title: A checked vehicle is not a verified fact: separate progress from evidence
item.description: The author of LeonidaRides, an indie game vehicle reference tool, explains a design rule: a player checking an item off is not the same as an editor verifying a fact, so progress and evidence stay separate.

item.title: Hydrilla AI tutorial: how much does one 3D asset actually cost? The $0.12 per prop math
item.description: This independent tutorial works through Hydrilla AI's official pricing page, FAQ, and Terms of Service to break down the roughly $0.12 cost of a single 3D prop, helping developers judge whether AI-generated assets are actually worth it.

item.title: Zombies Aren't Real Wiki - Complete Beginner Guide & Defense Strategies
item.description: A beginner's guide roundup for Zombies Aren't Real, a horde-defense tactical game, covering civilian evacuation and defense layouts.

item.title: One rules engine, two languages
item.description: Shows how CheX implements the chess rules engine twice — TypeScript in the browser and Rust on the server — and keeps both in exact agreement on every move, capture, and checkmate.

item.title: Modern Warfare 4 launch boosts Call of Duty HQ to top of Newzoo's PC revenue charts
item.description: The Modern Warfare 4 launch pushed Call of Duty HQ to the top of Newzoo's PC revenue chart, in a month with almost no other major releases.

item.title: Cheese Roll Game - Building a Fast 3D Browser Arcade Downhill Runner
item.description: The author shares how they built a fast, high-performance 3D browser arcade downhill runner with Three.js, covering optimization and game feel.

item.title: The MARROW Project
item.description: A developer is building a game engine called MARROW from scratch to learn how engines work under the hood, with plans to use it for an open-world game later.
